name: HAGAR detects the Crab Nebula at about 20 sigma with nine years of data

significance.quote: we report the detection of $\gamma$-rays from the Crab Nebula at a significance level of about 20$\sigma$,

summary.plain: Nine years of HAGAR observations of the Crab Nebula, about 219 hours, show gamma rays above 230 GeV at a significance of about 20 sigma and track the long-term performance of the array.
summary.technical: About 219 hours of Crab data from October 2008 to December 2017 analysed with the wavefront-sampling technique: detection at about 20 sigma, time-averaged flux (1.64 +- 0.09) x 10^-10 photons cm^-2 s^-1 above 230 GeV; study of systematic effects of the analysis.

title: VHE Gamma-ray Observation of Crab Nebula with HAGAR Telescope Array
why_it_matters: The abstract frames the Crab observations as an assessment of the performance of the HAGAR telescopes.
